claim: TIGAR was originally identified as a p53-inducible protein that functions as a fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase (F2,6P).
source: TIGAR (Tp53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator) was originally identified as a p53-inducible protein that functions as a fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase (F2,6P) but subsequently shown to have phosphatase activities for a variety of phosphorylated metabolic intermediates and allosteric regulators including 2,3-bisphospholgycerate (2,3BPG), 2-phosphoglycerate, phosphoglycolate, and phosphoenolpyruvate (Bensaad et al., 2006; Rigden, 2008; Bolaños, 2014; Tang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature (Bensaad et al., 2006; Rigden, 2008; Bolaños, 2014; Tang et al., 2021)

claim: TIGAR has phosphatase activities for 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3BPG), 2-phosphoglycerate, phosphoglycolate, and phosphoenolpyruvate.
source: TIGAR (Tp53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator) was originally identified as a p53-inducible protein that functions as a fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase (F2,6P) but subsequently shown to have phosphatase activities for a variety of phosphorylated metabolic intermediates and allosteric regulators including 2,3-bisphospholgycerate (2,3BPG), 2-phosphoglycerate, phosphoglycolate, and phosphoenolpyruvate (Bensaad et al., 2006; Rigden, 2008; Bolaños, 2014; Tang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature (Bensaad et al., 2006; Rigden, 2008; Bolaños, 2014; Tang et al., 2021)

claim: TIGAR is generally considered a suppressor of glycolysis because F2,6P is a potent allosteric activator for 6-phosphofructo-1-kinase (PFK1), the rate-limiting step in glycolysis.
source: Due to its F2,6P dephosphorylation activity, TIGAR is generally considered a suppressor of glycolysis as F2,6P is a potent allosteric activator for 6-phosphofructo-1-kinase (PFK1), the rate-limiting step in glycolysis.
evidence: Based on established biochemical knowledge about F2,6P and PFK1 function

claim: The dephosphorylation of 2,3BPG to generate 3-phosphoglycerate would be expected to increase glycolysis.
source: However, the dephosphorylation of 2,3BPG to generate 3-phosphoglycerate would also be expected to increase glycolysis (Bolaños, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature (Bolaños, 2014) and inference from metabolic pathway knowledge

claim: TIGAR expression protects against ischemic/reperfusion injury in the brain.
source: For example, in the brain TIGAR expression was reported to protect against ischemic/reperfusion injury (Li et al., 2021), whereas in the heart TIGAR deficiency protected myocardial infarction (Hoshino et al., 2012) and in pressure-overloaded hearts (Okawa et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature (Li et al., 2021)

claim: TIGAR deficiency protects against myocardial infarction in the heart.
source: For example, in the brain TIGAR expression was reported to protect against ischemic/reperfusion injury (Li et al., 2021), whereas in the heart TIGAR deficiency protected myocardial infarction (Hoshino et al., 2012) and in pressure-overloaded hearts (Okawa et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature (Hoshino et al., 2012)

claim: TIGAR deficiency protects pressure-overloaded hearts.
source: For example, in the brain TIGAR expression was reported to protect against ischemic/reperfusion injury (Li et al., 2021), whereas in the heart TIGAR deficiency protected myocardial infarction (Hoshino et al., 2012) and in pressure-overloaded hearts (Okawa et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature (Okawa et al., 2019)

claim: TIGAR can both enhance the development of premalignances and suppress the metastasis of cancer invasion by inhibiting ROS production.
source: Recently, it has been reported that TIGAR can both enhance the development of premalignances and suppress the metastasis of cancer invasion by the way of inhibition of ROS production (Cheung et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature (Cheung et al., 2020)

claim: TIGAR deficiency in cholinergic neurons results in marked protection against hypothermia following an acute cold challenge.
source: Surprisingly, we have observed that TIGAR deficiency in cholinergic neurons of mice results in a marked protection against hypothermia following an acute cold challenge.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Enhanced acetylcholine levels and increased cholinergic signaling at the neuromuscular junction drive skeletal muscle shivering-induced thermogenesis in TIGAR-deficient cholinergic neurons.
source: At a molecular level, this results from enhanced acetylcholine levels and increased cholinergic signaling at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) driving skeletal muscle shivering-induced thermogenesis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Whole-body TKO male mice display less than a 1°C decline in core body temperature during 1 hr acute cold exposure at 4°C.
